name: CWR Hawaii Inc
old_description: Hawaii’s premier full line rigging shop serving the islands and Pacific Rim since 1976. Our goal is to provide quality rigging products and hardware value priced with an excellent turnaround time. Our extensive cutting edge inventory and well trained knowledgeable sales staff are ready to meet all of your lifting, pulling, and load securing needs.
about:
CWR Hawaii Inc has operated as a locally owned rigging specialist in Honolulu, Hawaii since 1976. The company serves the Hawaiian islands and the broader Pacific Rim from its Honolulu base.

The shop functions as a full-line rigging fabricator and service provider. It maintains the largest wire rope swage press in the state and produces custom wire rope, chain, synthetic, and high-performance slings with working loads up to 500,000 pounds. In-house capabilities include proof testing up to 750,000 pounds, static and dynamic load testing of hoists up to 25 tons, and onsite resin pour sockets using Crosby Wirelock resin. The company also operates an authorized repair station for brands such as Harrington Hoists, Ingersoll-Rand, JET, and Columbus-McKinnon, and offers wire rope pressure lubrication via Kirkpatrick systems. Rental inventory includes wireless load cells ranging from 2.5 to 55 tons, a 6.5-ton Bluetooth load cell, and a Straightpoint Colt tension meter.

CWR Hawaii supports marine, industrial, and material-handling customers across the Pacific. Its fabrication and repair services meet OSHA and ASME standards, and the company provides onsite consultation, certified product training, and same-day turnaround for many fabrication requests.

The company emphasizes its local presence, ISO 9001 certification, and the ability to deploy personnel and equipment to job sites the same day. Its differentiators include the state's largest swage press, OEM-certified repair technicians, and a stock of rigging hardware that enables immediate shipment or fabrication.

name: Cable Associates
old_description: Founded in 1989, Cable Associates is a trusted USA custom cable assembly manufacturer specializing in Custom Harnesses, Fiber Optic - Copper - RF Cable Assemblies and Contract Manufacturing located in Archbald, Pennsylvania.
about:
Cable Associates was founded in 1989 in Archbald, Pennsylvania, as a U.S.-based cable manufacturer focused on quality, competitive pricing, customer service, and quick turnaround. The company began with a staff of under 10 and has grown to over 100 employees while maintaining its original core principles.

The company specializes in custom cable assemblies, including wire harnesses, fiber optic, copper, and RF cable assemblies, as well as contract manufacturing services. Its production capabilities encompass cutting, stripping, crimping, soldering, fiber polishing, epoxy dispensing, and comprehensive testing using equipment such as Schleuniger and Komax cut-and-strip machines, TE and Molex crimp presses, and Viavi optical test systems. All electrical assemblies undergo 100% continuity and signal integrity testing, while fiber optic and RF assemblies are tested to customer-specific requirements.

Cable Associates serves a diverse set of industries: military and aerospace (supplying defense contractors such as Leonardo DRS and Lockheed Martin), communications and telecom (supporting broadband expansion, FTTX, and data center upgrades), industrial, utilities (transmission and distribution networks), energy (wind, solar, electrical), medical (UL-rated assemblies), automotive (UL-rated harnesses), and agriculture (vehicle and machinery harnesses).

The company attributes its 35-plus-year customer retention to its unwavering commitment to U.S. manufacturing, quality certifications (AS9003, ITAR, UL, IPC standards), and rapid turnaround. It also holds an MMC Certification for hyperscale AI connectivity and is an authorized distributor for Microcare Sticklers fiber optic cleaning products.

about:
Cable Depot, Inc. was founded in 1990 in Norcross, Georgia, on principles of hard work, honesty, integrity, dedication, and strong relationships. The company describes its ethos as "The Spirit of Service," aiming to earn and retain customer trust.

The company manufactures custom and standard cable and fiber optic assemblies, including telco cables, custom molded cables, RF cables, SAS/SATA cables, IDC ribbon cables, and electromechanical assemblies. It offers custom cable design, prototyping, and manufacturing, with over 3,500 standard cable and interconnect products stocked. Production covers copper and fiber optic cable assemblies, harnesses, adapters, and connectivity products, supported by advanced equipment and a zero-defect quality program.

Cable Depot serves the medical, electronics, automotive, telecom, military (Mil Spec), robotics, instrumentation, audio, marine, and industrial markets. Its customers include OEMs, resellers, and engineering firms that rely on the company for data, voice, and video connectivity solutions.

The company emphasizes a rigorous zero-defects QA program, 100% product testing and guarantee, advanced equipment and tooling, engineering and prototyping support, on-time delivery, and competitive pricing as key differentiators.

name: Calumet Electronics
old_description: Calumet Electronics Corporation is a printed circuit board manufacturer headquartered in Calumet, Michigan, specializing in high-reliability PCBs for aerospace, defense, and medical device applications.
about:
Calumet Electronics Corporation was founded in 1968 in Calumet, Michigan, in the state's Upper Peninsula. The company has remained 100% American owned and operated since its inception, with no offshoring or brokering of production.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures high-reliability printed circuit boards from a 160,000-square-foot facility. Its capabilities span conventional, HDI, and HDBU fabrication, including 6- to 30-layer high-density multilayer packages with blind and buried vias, stacked microvias, and buried passives. Processes include sequential lamination (up to five or more cycles), bridge plating, via-in-pad (non-conductive, conductive, and copper-filled), laser and LED direct imaging, digital solder mask and silkscreen, mechanical milling, and edge castellation. The shop handles panel sizes up to 19.5 by 22.5 inches and supports copper weights up to 5 oz plated.

Calumet serves aerospace, defense, medical device, communications, electric power, industrial controls, space, and national security sectors. Its boards are used in U.S. military equipment, electric power grid protection, space applications, and life-saving medical devices.

The company emphasizes its fully domestic supply chain—design, engineering, and manufacturing all occur in the U.S. with no offshoring. It positions itself as a safe harbor for American electronics companies and has received Department of Defense funding to advance PCB technology. Its focus is on zero-defect reliability for mission-critical applications.

name: Chicago Plastic Systems
old_description: Chicago Plastic Systems' greatest asset is it's employees.  Although you've undoubtedly heard that from other companies, our organization was founded with this philosophy from the beginning and holds true today. Most of our employees are hired based on a referral from one of our current employees or business partners. This builds an environment that feels like family and a staff that functions as a team. In addition, because our employees are truly made to feel they're part of something bigger than themselves, they take great pride in every aspect of our business. As a result, our customers get the benefits of increased productivity and superior workmanship.
about:
Chicago Plastic Systems is headquartered in Neenah, Wisconsin, with a second facility in Crystal Lake, Illinois. The company was founded in September 1995 by three businessmen—Dirk Howell, John Stewart, and Leif Heggem—who started in Howell’s garage producing CPVC fittings for the metal finishing industry. The business is veteran-owned.

The company specializes in industrial thermoplastic fabrication, offering plastic machining, plastic welding, custom fabrication of tanks, process skids, pipe systems, ductwork, enclosures, and corrosion-resistant ventilation equipment. Operations span 107,000 square feet across two locations, with a staff of approximately 50 employees. Fabricators are DVS certified or in certification, and the shop includes multiple CNC machines, a large CNC butt welder, and one of the largest brake presses dedicated to plastic bending.

Chicago Plastic Systems serves industries including metal finishing, water treatment, chemical processing, power generation, semiconductor, food, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Customers range from OEMs needing custom thermoplastic components to plants requiring integrated installation and maintenance of fabricated systems.

The founders established the company on a philosophy of servant leadership, emphasizing dignity, honesty, and trust in relationships with customers, vendors, and employees. The firm highlights its commitment to DVS certification for all fabricators—a distinction it claims is unique in the U.S.—and a team-based culture built on employee referrals and long-tenured staff.

about:
Cirtronics Corporation, a contract manufacturer based in Milford, New Hampshire, was founded in 1979 by Gerardine Ferlins. Ferlins aimed to build a company that valued people as much as profits, extending that focus to customers, community, and suppliers. The company operates under an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), making every employee a part-owner.

The company provides end-to-end manufacturing services for complex electromechanical systems, including engineering support, supply chain management, production, testing, logistics, and repair and refurbishment. Its capabilities span full system integration, complex sub-assemblies, and board-level assembly. Cirtronics emphasizes lean manufacturing practices, with green belts on staff, and uses an integrated IT platform to deliver real-time production information and work instructions.

Cirtronics serves the robotics, medical and life sciences, defense and security, and industrial markets. Its customer base includes Ava Robotics, Image Stream Medical, Doble Engineering, Heller Industries, Rapiscan Systems, and Belmont Medical Technologies. The company also operates as a repair depot and refurbishment center, housing spares and providing upgrades for deployed products.

Cirtronics differentiates itself through its employee-ownership culture, which it says aligns the interests of customers and staff, fostering better communication and dedicated teamwork. The company's "Precision Engagement" approach tailors manufacturing programs to each client, and its quality management system monitors key processes with statistical process control. A focus on design for manufacturability and supplier qualification aims to reduce total cost of ownership.

name: Claremont Foods
old_description: Founded in 2011, we are a family-owned food manufacturing company, based in Colorado, whose core focus is quality and excellence. We have built our business on a foundation of trust and transparency, to best serve our clients, our team members and our community. We are proud to say that our team is made up of talented individuals who are passionate about what they do and committed to our company values.
about:
Claremont Foods was founded in 2011 in Westminster, Colorado, as a family-owned food manufacturing company. The business was started by Alex (CEO), his wife Allison (Controller), and Alex’s two brothers, Adam (CFO) and Greg (Board Member). The family’s passion for healthy eating and commitment to quality and excellence shaped the company’s culture from the outset.

The company operates a 135,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility where it provides a full suite of services: product innovation and development, materials sourcing, production and manufacturing, and product quality management. In-house capabilities include bench-top formulations, raw-material sourcing, costing analysis, line trials on existing equipment, packaging design, and access to external consultants. The team specializes in developing and producing energy bars, protein bars, and nutrition bars, using a transparent, volume-based tolling pricing model.

Claremont serves well-established brands in the food and natural-products industries that have national distribution. Its client base includes companies seeking new product development, cost reduction through re-formulation, packaging modifications, or process improvements, and quality enhancement of existing products. The company positions itself as an extension of the brand’s manufacturing division, handling supply-chain management so clients can focus on marketing and sales.

The founders emphasize mutual success, trust, and transparency as core differentiators. Because the family owners are directly involved in daily operations, clients interact with decision makers. The location adjacent to Boulder County—known as the heart of the natural-products industry—provides access to collective expertise, resources, and emerging innovations. A quality-assurance department staffed by SQF- and PCQI-certified professionals oversees every production shift.

name: Classic Packaging Company
old_description: Our top-of-the-line technologies allow us to offer a wide variety of packaging configurations and options to retailers, food processors, and packaging distributors across the nation. We design the best packaging solutions to your packaging needs.
about:
Classic Packaging Company operates from Pfafftown, North Carolina, where it has been family-owned and operated since its founding in 1991. The company began as a flexible packaging provider focused on delivering high-quality plastic packaging solutions to retailers, food processors, and distributors nationwide.

The company specializes in flexographic printing, laminating, coating, slitting, pouching, and bag making, supported by pre-press services and in-house lab testing. Its production floor runs 10-color PCMC flexographic presses with AVT 100% inspection, solventless single-component laminators from Nordmechanica and Comexi, and servo-driven pouch lines equipped with leak testers on every station. Additional capabilities include the Hudson-Sharp EZ-Stand system for pre-gusseted stand-up pouches and the INNO-LOK pre-zippered fastener application.

Classic Packaging serves retailers, food processors, and packaging distributors across the United States. Its food-grade, FDA-approved packaging is used for frozen foods, snacks, sweets, pet foods, frozen poultry, baking mixes, frozen vegetables, frozen seafood, and coffee. The company also supplies packaging distributors who resell its bags and pouches to end users.

The company states its mission is to create business relationships where all participants prosper, emphasizing honesty, integrity, a safe workplace, and environmental stewardship. It differentiates itself through continuous technological investment, rigorous quality control during lamination and printing, and proprietary equipment configurations that enable faster filling speeds and reduced waste.

The facility operates under an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system and employs statistical process control (SPC) with decades of accumulated process data.

Classic Sheet Metal serves as a supply-chain partner for several well-known global companies across a broad geographic footprint that includes the Midwest, South, and Mountain West regions. Specific industry sectors or named customers are not disclosed in public materials.

name: Commercial Cabling Company
old_description: Founded by Jeff and Ryan, Commercial Cabling Company brings over three decades of hands-on experience from the trading floors of the Chicago Board of Trade and the New York Stock Exchange to commercial facilities nationwide.
about:
Commercial Cabling Company is headquartered in Mesa, Arizona, and was founded in May 2014 as an SBA-certified Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB). Co-owners Jeff Geiselhofer and Ryan Geiselhofer launched the company after Jeff spent decades executing precision installations on the trading floors of the Chicago Board of Trade, the New York Stock Exchange, and the CME Group — environments where a single failed connection could trigger a financial crisis. Ryan holds majority ownership and drives operations and business development, while Jeff serves as lead technician.

The company designs and installs structured cabling, fiber optic networks, and full low-voltage infrastructure for commercial facilities across Arizona, Nevada, and nationwide. Services include Cat5e, Cat6, and Cat6A copper cabling; fiber optic cabling; wireless access point installation; security camera (CCTV) cabling; sound masking systems; access control and intrusion detection pre-wiring; and MDF/IDF buildouts with rack installation and cable management. Every run is tested with Fluke certification equipment to TIA/EIA-568 and ANSI/TIA-606 standards, documented, and backed by a lifetime craftsmanship warranty. A proprietary mobile installation system — a fully equipped, pre-organized tooling and materials platform on wheels — allows smaller elite crews to mobilize at full capacity from the first hour on site.

Clients span corporate offices and call centers, data centers, healthcare and medical facilities, educational institutions, manufacturing and industrial plants, and government and municipal buildings. The firm works directly with IT leaders, facilities directors, and construction teams, and its WOSB designation supports government procurement compliance. Notable projects referenced include a 20,000 sq. ft. facility security and access control installation in Gilbert and a 43-desk office cabling setup.

The company was built on the premise that most contractors cut corners — pulling cable, labeling a few ports, and moving on — and that the consequences of substandard structured cabling appear slowly, expensively, and at the worst possible time. Jeff’s trading-floor experience established a standard where "close enough is not a category." The ownership model, mobile inventory system, and same-day emergency response capability are all structured to deliver predictable, documented quality without disrupting client operations.
